messages:
Alex: Morning — quick async check. What I did: landed routing-policy change to prefer regional pools for low-latency customers (PR: https://git.redwood/infra/merge/512). Blockers: noticed a small spike in 429s in staging during canary. Today: follow up on canary traffic split and watch metrics. :eyes:
Priya: ✅ saw the PR, nice. What I did: updated auth middleware to propagate tenant-id to the routing layer, added unit tests. Blockers: failing e2e around session refresh in the jwt rotation branch. Today: debug jwt rotation e2e and open a fix. :lock:
Marco: I reproduced the 429s — looks like batcher sizing hit a boundary when seq-lens spiked. Quick repro: `ab -n 200 -c 20 http://staging-gw/api/generate?model=redwood-lite` gave ~8% 429s. Investigating batching window logic now. :warning:
Jen: What I did: reviewed two gateway PRs (512, 515). Blockers: need a small change on 515 to add fallback model mapping for regional miss. Today: I'll push that patch and request a re-review. Please ping me if you're pairing. :thumbsup:
Sam: Heads up — auth key rotation is scheduled tonight 02:00 UTC. I added a deployment window and a runbook in ops-docs. If the jwt refresh bug isn't fixed before then we should postpone. See https://confluence.redwood/ops/jwt-rotation. :calendar:
Alex: Good call, @Sam. If Priya's fix isn't green by 01:30 UTC let's hold rotation. @Marco can you prioritize a staging load test after your batching tweak?
Marco: Yep, will run a staged load with variable sequence lengths (short/long mix). ETA 45m. I'll post results here.
Priya: Working on the e2e now. Found the race: session cache TTL + concurrent refresh. Quick patch in branch jwt-rotation-fix. Pushed — https://git.redwood/infra/branch/jwt-rotation-fix. Hoping tests pass.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for infra/gateway v1.22.3 -> 10% traffic. Rollout ID: canary-2026-03-17-01. Status: in-progress. :rocket:
Jen: If canary shows 429 regression we should automate automatic fallback to older instance group. Can we add a temporary routing policy rule to route traffic away from canary on 429 rate?
Alex: We already have an automatic fallback policy but it's conservative. @Jen suggest an emergency rule: if 429 rate > 5% for 5m then shift 20% away from canary. Who can own that tweak?
Sam: I can add the tweak to the routing-policy config and gate it with a feature flag. Will submit small PR and notify SRE.
Marco: Load test results: after increasing batching-window by 10ms, 429s dropped to ~1.2% under the same spike scenario. I'll post charts in a sec.
Priya: Tests turned green on jwt-rotation-fix. Merged and triggered staging deploy.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-03-17-01: progressed to 40% traffic. No fatal errors detected.
Alex: Great. Action items: (1) Sam to open quick PR for 429 emergency routing rule (2) Jen to prepare rollback notes in case canary worsens (3) Marco to add the batching tweak to the PR for the runtime optimizer (4) Priya to monitor auth rotation deploy. I'll keep an eye on dashboards. Ping here if anything spikes. :white_check_mark:
Jen: I'll have rollback notes in 15m. Also tagging @alex for postmortem template if we need it.
Sam: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/merge/518 — includes feature flag.
Alex: Thanks team — I'll be offline in ~2h but reachable on phone for urgent alerts.
